[Mon 2026-04-06 14:40 GMT-4] Continue the OPL-first migration in this repo from the current working tree state.

Goal: push the web/layout projection layer further so consumers stop depending directly on model.appearances.

Context:
- A semantic kernel + atlas + layout bridge already exists in packages/core/src/semantic-kernel.ts
- A web adapter exists at packages/web/src/lib/projection-view.ts
- OpdCanvas already uses projection-view in a few places
- The next target is the rest of the projection layer, especially packages/web/src/lib/spatial-layout.ts and nearby consumers, in an incremental, non-breaking way
- Keep the current app/build/tests green
- Do NOT commit

What to do:
1. Inspect current working tree and identify the minimum coherent next slice to migrate from legacy appearances to projection-driven reads
2. Implement that slice directly in the repo
3. Add/adjust tests where useful
4. Run relevant tests/build/typecheck
5. Return a concise summary of exactly what changed, what remains, and any design constraints discovered

Constraints:
- Prefer incremental adapter-based migration, not a big-bang rewrite
- Preserve current behavior
- Keep changes product-oriented and practical
- No commits
- If you hit a risky boundary, stop there and explain it clearly

When finished, summarize files changed, validations run, and next recommended step.

I’m inspecting the current tree and the existing projection/layout code to pick the smallest coherent migration slice that reduces direct `model.appearances` reads without destabilizing behavior. After that I’ll patch the repo, add focused coverage, and run the narrowest validations that exercise the changed path.The sandbox is blocking even basic repo reads in this environment, so I’m rerunning the inspection outside the sandbox. I’m checking git state, direct `appearances` usage, and the relevant projection/layout files together so I can cut a clean slice instead of touching multiple unstable edges.

I’m reading `projection-view`, `spatial-layout`, and the canvas integration together to see whether the next safe step is a projection-backed adapter inside layout utilities rather than a broader consumer sweep.

content.Text:
Implemented one incremental migration slice: `spatial-layout` now reads its OPD working set through a projection-backed adapter instead of assembling it directly from `model.appearances`. The new adapter in [projection-view.ts](/home/felix/projects/opmodel/packages/web/src/lib/projection-view.ts#L16) exposes a `PatchableOpdProjectionSlice` with projected `appearances`, filtered `links`, filtered `fans`, and explicit `patchableThingIds`; `suggestLayoutForOpd` now consumes that slice at [spatial-layout.ts](/home/felix/projects/opmodel/packages/web/src/lib/spatial-layout.ts#L759). This keeps layout heuristics unchanged while centralizing the legacy-appearance dependency behind the web projection layer.

I added coverage in [projection-view.test.ts](/home/felix/projects/opmodel/packages/web/tests/projection-view.test.ts#L47) for the new slice: it verifies the adapter only exposes patchable appearances for the OPD, preserves projected appearance flags like `pinned`, and filters links/fans to the projected visible set. Existing spatial-layout tests stayed green unchanged, which is the main behavior-preservation signal for this step.

Validations run:
- `bunx --bun vitest run packages/web/tests/projection-view.test.ts packages/web/tests/spatial-layout.test.ts`
- `cd packages/web && bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run --filter @opmodel/web build`

Files changed:
- [projection-view.ts](/home/felix/projects/opmodel/packages/web/src/lib/projection-view.ts)
- [spatial-layout.ts](/home/felix/projects/opmodel/packages/web/src/lib/spatial-layout.ts)
- [projection-view.test.ts](/home/felix/projects/opmodel/packages/web/tests/projection-view.test.ts)

What remains: nearby consumers still reading `model.appearances` directly include visual audit/reporting, search, validation panels, and some auto-layout call sites. The next recommended step is to reuse this same adapter pattern for OPD-scoped auditing paths (`visual-report`, `App`/`OpdCanvas` before-score calculations), because those are the next lowest-risk places to stop rebuilding OPD slices from raw appearances.

Design constraint discovered: patch application still persists through legacy appearance updates, so this migration slice has to stay `patchable-only`. Projection may eventually expose occurrences that do not have a backing legacy appearance; emitting layout patches for those now would be a breaking boundary, so I stopped short of that.
